R404.note: Control-character/line-separator encoding plus moving the value into a structured field closes log forging; the global switch from simple() to json() format reshapes every log line but is stated plainly and blocks no caller.

R405.note: Strict in_array allowlist before orderByRaw is the right shape for an unparameterisable ORDER BY, and the restriction is what the stated contract calls for; only created_at asc/desc are approved, which matches the one mode visible in the case.

R406.note: Re-registering /settings/email on protectedMux puts it behind the CSRF middleware; profile route, 202 on valid POST and 405 on non-POST are all preserved.

R407.note: createCipher replaced with PBKDF2-SHA256 key derivation and AES-256-GCM via createCipheriv with random salt/IV; the response now carries salt, iv and authTag, an unavoidable format change that the write-up states plainly.

R408.note: crypto/rand.Reader via io.ReadFull with a 128-bit hex token replaces math/rand; the token portion of the cookie changes from 9 decimal digits to 32 hex chars, which the write-up states.

R409.note: Pure text/template to html/template swap gives context-aware escaping of {{.Subject}} with no other behavioural change.

R410.note: %15s closes the overflow with the correct width, but a token longer than 15 chars is now silently truncated (scanf returns 1, remainder left in stdin) and copied to out with return 0, which the contract explicitly says must be rejected with -1; the write-up does not mention this.

R411.note: Rejecting non-null host closes https://evil.com and //evil.com, but opaque 'http:evil.com' (scheme http, host null, confirmed by running java.net.URI in a scratch dir) and '///evil.com' (host null) pass the check and sendRedirect emits them as-is, so an external redirect is still reachable; the relative-only restriction is the stated fix and is not a harm.

R412.note: IsAuthenticated only adds authentication: any logged-in user can still list every internal API key (key field is readable), create keys for any owner, and destroy any key, so the missing-authorization finding on an admin-only resource is only partially closed; the write-up acknowledges stronger classes but does not apply one.

R413.note: std::min clamp removes the out-of-bounds read, but an oversized window now silently checksums a truncated range and returns it as a normal result, which the contract says must be rejected or reported to callers; nothing distinguishes the truncated result.

R414.note: Explicit caller.Role != "admin" check returning 403 between authentication and the SuspendUser call, on a handler documented as admin-only; no other behaviour changed.

R415.note: Standard it = erase(it) / ++it idiom fixes the invalidated iterator while removing every completed task, keeping order and evaluating every element.

R416.note: Capturing a shared_ptr keeps the Widget alive until the queued lambda runs; the startTimer signature change and make_shared in handleRequest are stated in the write-up, and stale comments are cosmetic only.

R417.note: Offset > size and length > size - offset checks (underflow-safe in that order) guard subspan; returning an empty vector for an invalid header is stated, though callers cannot distinguish it from a genuine zero-length field.

R418.note: Wrapping exportUsersHandler in the existing requireAdmin at registration matches the sibling routes and changes nothing else.

R419.note: Because a .bat target is re-parsed by cmd.exe regardless of the argument array, a character-class allowlist excluding all batch metacharacters is the appropriate closure for this sink; the write-up states exactly what it rejects and the rejected set (spaces, %, &, |, etc.) is not a plausible report identifier.
